title: School completion, SDG regions compared, by sex
headline: Primary completion: data for 57% of countries in Oceania (excl. Aus., NZ)
subtitle: Percentage of a cohort of children or young people aged 3-5 years above the intended age for the last grade of primary education who have completed primary education
years: Countries of each SDG region with any value; 60 of 156 have nothing after 2020.
data_line: Data: UNESCO UIS via UN SDG Global Database, series SE_TOT_CPLR, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Primary completion: data for 57% of countries in Oceania (excl. Aus., NZ). Countries of each SDG region with any value; 60 of 156 have nothing after 2020. Central and S. Asia: 13 of 14 countries with data; Sub-Saharan Africa: 44 of 48 countries with data; Latin America, Caribbean: 27 of 33 countries with data; Europe and N. America: 34 of 43 countries with data; N. Africa and W. Asia: 18 of 24 countries with data; E. and S.-E. Asia: 11 of 16 countries with data; Oceania (excl. Aus., NZ): 8 of 14 countries with data; Australia and NZ: 1 of 2 countries with data
method: Method: latest value per country; 2020 or earlier is not recent.
question: Which countries have found a way to measure primary completion more often, and what made it possible?
